channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: One person died from West Nile virus infection in the Netherlands
item.description: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported on Friday that 12 European countries have reported cases of West Nile virus this year.

item.title: New bluefin tuna farms in the Mediterranean Sea threaten global food security
item.description: “Atlantic bluefin tune can swim 260 kilometers every day so it is cruel and unnatural to confine them in sea cages.”

item.title: Belgian city ranked as second most beautiful summer city of Europe
item.description: The city's waterways, traditional architecture and historic attractions make it no surprise that it ranks so highly.

item.title: Three best European cities where you can work while on holidays
item.description: A new ranking has revealed the best European cities for combining remote work with a trip abroad, based on internet speeds, costs, coworking spaces and "things to do".

item.title: Almost all households in Gaza in need of shelter aid
item.description: "The materials needed to repair homes and provide improved shelters are still not entering Gaza at anything close to the scale required."

item.title: Netherlands: Several people injured after coach carrying students crashes on motorway
item.description: The coach was reportedly carrying 54 students and four teachers from a German state school. They were on their way to Paris.

item.title: Italy and German clash again over irregular migration in Mediterranean
item.description: Deputy PM Matteo Salvini said Italy would not accept the return of any irregular migrants while German aid NGOs remain active in the Mediterranean.

item.title: Putin says Ukraine 'has opened Pandora's box' with its recent attacks in rare interview
item.description: In an interview broadcast on Saturday, Putin said Kyiv had now “let the genie out of the bottle”.

item.title: Commission withholds information about protection of unaccompanied minors in Ceuta
item.description: “Unaccompanied minors are excluded from accelerated asylum and return procedures.“

item.title: TikTok's European division posts its first profit, but lawsuits are costing a lot
item.description: Online sales through TikTok and streaming activities contributed to stronger earnings, but the company reserved over €850 million for legal matters.

item.title: Deadly 5.9 magnitude earthquake erupts in Japanese Tokyo region
item.description: At least 699 houses were completely destroyed and around 6,500 people are still staying in evacuation centres.

item.title: Musical instruments used by Freddie Mercury to be auctioned in London
item.description: Among the lots is a Yamaha C3 grand piano, which Mercury often used the instrument to compose solo material and some of Queen’s biggest songs.

item.title: Iranian hackers shut down British power plant
item.description: The attack may have been intended to demonstrate that hackers linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard can gain access to critical infrastructure.

item.title: Indonesia deploys 1,500 additional troops to fight wildfires raging in Borneo
item.description: Indonesian officials warned that the fire season has only just begun and is rapidly intensifying.

item.title: Swedish police reveal details of deadly school sword attack
item.description: An 18-year-old man armed with a sword entered the school on Friday, killing one person and injuring three others.

item.title: Japanese man leaves young child alone on the trail for 8 hours to pursue Fuji mountain climb
item.description: The boy was found alone on a hiking trail on Thursday and taken to a police station.

item.title: Two dead after tourist glider plane crash in Croatian mountains
item.description: The aircraft went down on Friday afternoon in the Velebit mountain range, near the Adriatic coast.

item.title: Water levels on the Rhine are slowly improving
item.description: Rain in southern Germany is slowly raising water levels on the Rhine after a record low, but normal conditions for inland shipping are not expected before late September or early October.

item.title: UN coordinator warns of unprecedented spread of Ebola in Congo
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading at an exceptional rate and has killed more than 2,500 people, the United Nations has warned.

item.title: Virgin one step closer to operating trains to rival Eurostar
item.description: Competition for Eurostar is gradually taking shape, but Virgin still has a long way to go.
